controls: A reported periodic result is above the ELV
Assess compliance by subtracting the applicable measurement uncertainty from the measured value.
Treating every raw exceedance as an automatic breach
The uncertainty-adjusted result remains above the ELV
Classify it as likely to be an ELV breach, subject to the regulator's full assessment.
The raw result is above the ELV but the uncertainty-adjusted result is below it
Treat it as approaching the limit rather than breaching it under the stated general approach.
Calling an uncertainty-adjusted compliant value a breach
The reported result is already below the ELV
Do not perform the exceedance compliance adjustment using measurement uncertainty.
Measurement uncertainty is used for ELV compliance
Use expanded uncertainty at a 95% confidence interval.
Periodic particulate matter is assessed at or above the ELV
Use a maximum uncertainty of 20%, or 1 mg/m3 where the ELV is below 5 mg/m3.
